entities.summary: Po Saktiray Daputih was the king of Champa who ruled from 1695 to 1728. He played a crucial role in the expansion of the Champa Empire, which at its peak spanned across present-day central Vietnam. Po Saktiray Daputih's reign was marked by significant military campaigns, including the conquest of the neighboring kingdom of Dai Viet. His diplomatic efforts led to the establishment of trade relations with the Chinese Ming dynasty. The king's legacy extends beyond his territorial conquests, as he oversaw the development of Champa's unique blend of Hindu and Buddhist traditions. This cultural synthesis had a lasting impact on the region's artistic and architectural heritage. Po Saktiray Daputih's reign also saw the rise of Champa's powerful maritime trade networks, which connected the kingdom to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. Despite his military successes, Po Saktiray Daputih's reign was ultimately cut short by the arrival of the French colonizers in the 19th century. As a result, his legacy was all but forgotten until recent archaeological discoveries brought attention to the king's contributions to Champa's rich cultural heritage. Po Saktiray Daputih's story serves as a testament to the enduring power of Southeast Asian monarchies and their complex relationships with regional and global powers.
